date.note: arXiv submission date (v1, 23 March 2007). Published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 98, 211803 (2007).

name: Evidence for D⁰–D̅⁰ mixing

summary.plain: Belle reports evidence that a neutral D particle can turn into its own antiparticle ('mixing') before it decays, seen as a small difference in apparent lifetime between two kinds of D decay. The paper says its value is more than 3σ from zero, whereas earlier measurements averaged about 2σ above zero.
summary.technical: Measurement of y_CP = (1.31 ± 0.32(stat) ± 0.25(syst))% from lifetime differences between CP-eigenstate and flavour-eigenstate D⁰ decays in 540 fb⁻¹, 3.2σ from zero, with no evidence for CP violation.

title: Evidence for D⁰ – D̅⁰ Mixing
why_it_matters: The paper says mixing between a particle and its antiparticle had been observed in neutral kaons, B⁰ and, most recently, B_s mesons. In the Standard Model D-mixing is expected to be small, loop diagrams with new, as-yet-unobserved particles could significantly affect the measured values, and CP-violating effects in D-mixing would be a clear signal of new physics; Belle finds no evidence for CP violation.
